body:
Shorter approximate rotations save supplied T states

Here \(X,Y,Z\) are Pauli operators, \(R_z(\phi)=e^{-i\phi Z/2}\), and \(T=\operatorname{diag}(1,e^{i\pi/4})\). The target angle is \(\theta\). A symbol such as \(T_B\) counts T gates; it does not denote elapsed time.

The semiclassical inverse QFT needs 464 synthesized rotations. Reference [84] combines a cheap probabilistic attempt with a fallback, then mixes opposite angle errors. Use its convention \(Z_\theta=e^{i\theta Z}=R_z(-2\theta)\). Errors below are diamond norms of channels, so their bounds also cover entangled inputs and add across sequential replacements.

1. Pay for the long correction only on failure

Choose an exactly synthesizable unitary

\[V=\begin{pmatrix}u&-v^*\\v&u^*\end{pmatrix},\qquad |u|^2+|v|^2=1.\]
Ancilla resultBranch operatorResulting rotation
0, probability \(q=|u|^2\)\(K_0=\operatorname{diag}(u,u^*)\)\(Z_{\arg u}\), chosen near \(Z_\theta\)
1, probability \(1-q\)After Y: \(YK_1=-i\operatorname{diag}(v,v^*)\)\(Z_{\arg v}\); repair with \(B\approx Z_{\theta-\arg v}\)

The probabilities are input-independent. With successful-branch error \(\epsilon_1\) and repaired-failure error \(\epsilon_2\),

\[\epsilon_F\le\epsilon_1+(1-q)\epsilon_2,\qquad \mathbb E[T]=T_{\rm attempt}+(1-q)T_B.\]

A rare fallback can tolerate a looser approximation while contributing little expected T cost.

2. Cancel opposite coherent errors

Randomly choose \(Z_{\theta+\delta}\) or \(Z_{\theta-\delta}\) with equal probability. For any input density operator \(\rho\), removing the target rotation leaves

\[\tfrac12e^{i\delta Z}\rho e^{-i\delta Z}+\tfrac12e^{-i\delta Z}\rho e^{i\delta Z}=\cos^2\delta\,\rho+\sin^2\delta\,Z\rho Z.\]
One coherent error

Diamond error \(2|\sin\delta|\sim2|\delta|\).

Opposite errors mixed

The linear terms cancel; error \(2\sin^2\delta\sim2\delta^2\).

For unequal signed errors \(\delta_1\le0\le\delta_2\) and success probabilities \(q_1,q_2\), in the small-error regime \(|\delta_j|<\pi/4\), choose circuit 1 with probability

\[\pi=\frac{q_2\sin(2\delta_2)}{q_2\sin(2\delta_2)-q_1\sin(2\delta_1)}.\]

Writing \(\eta_j\) for the error of circuit j's corrected fallback, Theorem 3.17 bounds the mixture by

\[\epsilon_{\rm mix}\le2\pi q_1\sin^2\delta_1+2(1-\pi)q_2\sin^2\delta_2+\pi(1-q_1)\eta_1+(1-\pi)(1-q_2)\eta_2.\]

The displayed formula assumes a nonzero denominator. If both successful branches are exact, there is no linear error to cancel and either can be chosen. Here \(\pi\) is a classical circuit choice; \(q_j\) is a measurement success probability. The circuits are not coherently superposed.

3. Use the wider angle tolerance to find shorter sequences

Quadratic cancellation allows angle deviations of order \(\sqrt\epsilon\), increasing the supply of short candidates. Classical synthesis searches entries in the ring generated by \(i\) and \(1/\sqrt2\), solves the remaining norm equation, and converts the unitary to Clifford+T gates. Its fitted average cost, used by IonQ, is

\[C_T(\epsilon)\approx0.57\log_2(1/\epsilon)+8.83.\]

This is an empirical average, not a per-angle worst-case guarantee.

4. Balance approximation against faulty supplied states

Let \(\epsilon\) be the per-rotation diamond-norm error budget and \(C_T(\epsilon)\) the fitted T count. With \(N_R=464\) and accepted T-pair error \(p_{\rm pair}=1.30\times10^{-8}\), minimize

\[E(\epsilon)=\frac{N_Rp_{\rm pair}}2C_T(\epsilon)+N_R\epsilon,\qquad \epsilon_* =\frac{0.57p_{\rm pair}}{2\ln2}\approx5.35\times10^{-9}.\]

This matches the scale of the chosen \(5.30\times10^{-9}\). The reported average is 24.5 T gates per rotation; accounting uses 5,684 accepted pairs:

\[p_{\rm iQFT}\le\underbrace{5{,}684(1.30\times10^{-8})}_{\text{faulty T pairs}}+\underbrace{464(5.30\times10^{-9})}_{\text{approximation}}=7.64\times10^{-5}\quad\text{(rounded)}.\]

summary: Try a short approximate rotation, invoke a longer correction only on failure, and mix opposite angle errors. Their canceled linear error permits shorter synthesized circuits.
title: Mixed-fallback rotation synthesis: spend fewer T states
